# Education in China
Education in China has historically focused on improving population literacy, with enrollment significantly increasing across primary and secondary levels since the early years of the People's Republic of China. The system is guided by the Law on Nine-Year Compulsory Education (effective 1986), which mandates six years of primary education and three years of junior high school. This system integrates elementary and middle school education under the "Nine Years – One Policy," emphasizing continuity and local proximity.
Modern education policy, influenced by the Four Modernizations, has prioritized economic modernization, leading to increased focus on science, technology, and vocational skills. While the system has achieved remarkable global academic success in areas like the International Mathematical Olympiad, it faces criticisms regarding intense competition, an overemphasis on rote memorization and standardized testing (like the *Gaokao* ), and significant regional inequality between urban and rural areas. Furthermore, the curriculum is tightly controlled by the central government, ensuring alignment with the Chinese Communist Party's directives.
